correctness.rationale: One vacancy forces a full traversal of \(n-1\) unit-rate edges between independent regenerative special-bond crossings. The two-state gate-at-bond recursion gives \(\phi_{\rm on}=r(b+s)/Q\) and \(\phi_{\rm off}=rb/Q\); conditioning on the independent Gamma traversal proves the displayed transform. Differentiation gives both exact moments; the renewal reward theorem and a strictly decreasing integral prove current and monotonicity. Moment expansions yield the positive slow-limit current and divergent counting Fano factor, with a strictly sub-Poisson fast end. A separately assembled \(2n\)-state generator and killed generator passed 96 exact rational independent moment/current/Laplace checks across 24 parameter choices; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the complete finite-ring one-vacancy renewal transform and quantitative current/noise crossover for an independent telegraph bond, not the general renewal method or qualitative intermittency. Material from the primary dynamic-defect literature and the most directly relevant general gated-reaction papers was compared by model hypotheses and implication. No inspected paper establishes the stated combination; historical queueing or Markov-modulated transport may contain equivalent special cases, and search incompleteness remains an explicit risk.
residual_risks: Old queueing and Markov-modulated-service literature may have an equivalent renewal-time distribution or large Fano law under different terminology.
The general recurrence/renewal algebra is established prior mathematical machinery; originality attaches only to the precisely parameterized finite-ring classification.
Bibliographic searches and inspected literature are not exhaustive, and no independent expert originality assessment exists.

value.rationale: Current and long-time shot noise are natural experimentally interpretable transport invariants in finite exclusion systems with dynamic bottlenecks. The claim gives one exact normalized law, all-speed current monotonicity, precise slow- and fast-switching boundaries, and a forced Fano crossover. Most notably, arbitrarily amplified counting noise coexists with strictly positive finite mean current, distinguishing intermittent blockade from static effective-rate averaging. This is structural transport information beyond a trivial finite enumeration, while explicitly limited to the single-vacancy sector.
